QR codes, minus the browser.
FreeQrly speaks HTTP and MCP. Generate static QR codes from any agent, script, or workflow — no key, no sign-up, no expiry. If you can make a request, you can make a code.

Add https://freeqrly.com/mcp to your MCP client. generate_qr needs no auth; dynamic_qr_* tools manage your editable dynamic codes with an API token. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, and anything speaking Streamable HTTP.
A plain GET endpoint returning SVG. CORS is wide open, so browsers, curl, and serverless functions can all call it directly. Authenticated endpoints manage dynamic codes with a Bearer token.
A SKILL.md with payload recipes lives in the repo at skills/qr-generator/. Point your agent at it and it knows the rest.
/llms.txt describes the whole site for crawlers and assistants — endpoints, payload formats, and page map in one file.
Returns image/svg+xml. Only data is required; everything else has a sane default. Errors come back as JSON with an error field.
data — text to encode (required, max 2000 chars). URLs, WiFi strings, vCards, plain text.
ecc — error correction L, M, Q, H (default M). Use Q/H for print or logos.

Dynamic codes stay editable after printing and track scans — the same codes you manage in the dashboard, with the same quota (8 free). Create a token in the dashboard under API Tokens (shown once), then pass it as a Bearer token:

Tokens are per-user, revocable anytime from the dashboard, and deleted with your account. A token can never create or revoke other tokens — that requires a login session. Without a token these endpoints return 401; over quota returns 403 quota_exceeded.
Standard Streamable HTTP: initialize, then tools/list / tools/call. The generate_qr tool takes data, size, color, bgcolor, ecc and returns a ready-to-download SVG URL — no auth needed.

With an Authorization: Bearer header, five more tools appear: dynamic_qr_create, dynamic_qr_list, dynamic_qr_update, dynamic_qr_delete, dynamic_qr_stats — your editable dynamic codes, same quota as the dashboard.

It's free, but be kind: cache results instead of re-requesting the same code, and keep automated traffic reasonable. Per-IP rate limits apply. Static codes are deterministic — the same input always yields the same output, so caching is trivial.
